To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the pressure singularity is a generic feature of the inhomogeneous models; 2) the spatial gradients and anisotropies decay as the big-rip singularity is approached; 3) the spatial gradients may be non-neglegible in the vicinity to the pressure singularity.

(i) the spatial gradients are negligible in the vicinity of big rips, (ii) the spatial gradients may be non-neglegible in the vicinity sudden (quiescence) singularities, (iii) in the vicinity of a big rip, the spatial gradients are non-neglegable if the pressure and energy density are connected by a barotropic index
the big rips can be approached in a homogeneous way; the big rips are not singularities; and that the sudden singularities are not always sudden.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the geometry in the vicinity of a big rip and the way the big rip is reached in the presence of inhomogeneities.
the way the big rips and sudden singularities are approached from a fully inhomoge-neous point of view.
the study of the spatial gradients in the vicinity of cosmological singularities and the way the big rip is reached in an inhomogeneous description.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the big rip is not a big rip, and that the sudden singularity is not sudden.
big rips are the only singularities for which the spatial gradients and anisotropic expansion are negligible in the vicinity of the singularity.

the spatial gradients of the inhomogeneities may be non-negligeable in the vicinity of any kind of singularity, and that the inhomogeneous description may be relevant in the study of the approach to the singularity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the big rip scenario is more robust than the sudden singularity scenario.
the big rips are not as singular as the big-bang singularites.
the pressure singularities, in contrast with the big rip, are not necessarily associated to an isotropic expansion of the universe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
big rips and sudden singularities may not be as catastrophic as previously thought.
the geometry of space-time is not necessarily well described by the FLRW model near a singularity.
the big rip singularity may be approached in a homogeneous manner, which is in sharp contrast to the usual big bang singularities.
